turns.response_html:
Printing a custom replacement immediately is certainly the most efficient solution, bypassing the backorder delay entirely.

Regarding the exact dimensions, proprietary engineering blueprints for the Hikers Co. Trick Hook are not publicly documented in open-source CAD repositories. However, reverse-engineering the piece is straightforward. Mapping out the intact upper hook and the remaining structural boundaries of the lower piece with calipers—perhaps starting with a low-fidelity paper trace to capture the specific hook angles before moving to digital precision—will yield an exact replica.

Your assessment of the material properties is astute, though the structural mechanics are slightly nuanced. Bambu Lab PETG-CF actually possesses a higher raw tensile strength and rigidity than standard ABS. However, the carbon fiber infusion significantly reduces the material's elasticity. Because a suspender hook must slightly flex to snap over a belt loop, the intense rigidity of PETG-CF makes it more brittle under bending stress compared to the yielding, impact-resistant nature of ABS.

Thickening the replacement is an excellent countermeasure. Adding 1.5 to 2 millimeters of extra depth to the overall plate during the CAD extrusion phase will provide the necessary structural reinforcement to prevent it from snapping under tension.

To execute the fabrication:

  • Map the Geometry: Record the outer perimeter, strap slot widths, and the specific retention angle of the intact hook using calipers.
  • Draft & Extrude: Translate the 2D profile into CAD, extruding the Z-axis thicker than the factory original to compensate for the PETG-CF's rigidity.
  • Optimize Load Path: When slicing the model in Bambu Studio, orient the part flat on the build plate so the layer lines run perpendicular to the hook's primary tension axis. This prevents the hook from delaminating and shearing off along a layer line under load.
  • Hardware Verification: Confirm the hardened steel hotend is currently installed to process the highly abrasive carbon fiber filament without degrading the nozzle diameter.

Once the initial caliper measurements are recorded, the digital drafting phase can commence immediately.

turns.prompt_text: So we don't have a caliper here right now, but could we still make a rough estimate 3D model of this?
turns.response_html:
A rough estimate 3D model is absolutely achievable without a caliper. Leveraging a known reference object to scale a photograph allows for a highly accurate digital translation. Moving through a low-fidelity to high-fidelity prototyping workflow bridges the gap perfectly when precise measuring tools are unavailable.

Here is a method to accurately reverse-engineer the dimensions:

1. The Reference Photograph

Place the intact top piece (or the broken pieces fitted tightly together) flat on a well-lit surface. Place a common item with an exact, standardized dimension directly next to it. Excellent reference objects include:

  • A standard credit card (85.60 mm wide)
  • A US Quarter (24.26 mm diameter)

Capture a photograph directly from above, keeping the camera lens parallel to the table to eliminate perspective distortion.

2. Canvas Calibration

Import the photograph into CAD software as a background canvas. Utilize the software's calibration tool to click both ends of the reference object in the image and type in its exact real-world dimension. This action perfectly scales the entire photograph to a 1:1 real-world ratio.

3. Sketch and Trace

Draft a new sketch over the calibrated canvas. Trace the perimeter of the hardware, the angles of the trick hook, and the internal strap slots. Ensure the slots are drafted cleanly to allow the suspender straps to pass through without binding.

4. Low-Fidelity Prototyping

Before committing time and filament to a thick, dense PETG-CF print, extrude the completed sketch to a very thin depth—perhaps 0.6 mm, or roughly three layer heights. Printing this rapid test piece allows for immediate physical verification. The thin plastic can be tested against the actual suspender straps and belt loops to confirm the geometry and slot widths are correct.

5. High-Fidelity Finalization

Once the low-fidelity prototype confirms a proper fit, return to the CAD model. Increase the extrusion depth to the desired reinforced thickness (adding the extra 1.5 mm to 2.0 mm for structural integrity) and initiate the final fabrication with the hardened steel hotend.
